title: Dagster tracks which data produced which data but not who accepted a materialisation, or under which rule
content:
Dagster's lineage graph is about data: which asset was produced from which other asset, by which computation. That answers how a number came to exist. It does not record that a person accepted a materialisation, or the rule under which they were entitled to accept it.

The research states the split precisely — lineage answers 'how', while a decision record answers 'who and under what authority'. The two are not substitutes, and the distinction matters because only the second carries accountability. A pipeline can be perfectly reproducible and still leave nobody answerable for the output that was released downstream.

At Neurospace, whose work sits on Dagster, that makes the fit additive rather than competitive. Nothing about the lineage graph has to change. What is missing is a separate, attributed record of the human acceptance events that the orchestration already implies but never stores, which is a smaller ask than replacing any part of the data platform.
